original_test_intent: Verify the complete processor-related sensor population and every specified name, description and reading consistently across in-band SDR/Sensor List, out-of-band SDR/Sensor List and BMC Web against the authoritative processor-sensor specification.
original_method: Bind SUT, BMC and processor topology, retain complete unfiltered in-band and protected OOB SDR and Sensor List outputs at aligned timestamps, derive the CPU set only from an owner-approved sensor map, capture all BMC-Web pages, normalize names/descriptions/units/readings/status/thresholds and compare each required processor sensor across all representations while retaining anomaly logs.
manual_activity: The platform owner supplies processor topology/specification and resolves whether criteria 3–5 are omitted requirements or a numbering typo; an operator captures the complete BMC Web view and the owner decides the final result.
required_inputs: SUT/BMC/CPU socket, die, processor model and firmware identities
Authoritative processor sensor specification with all required names/descriptions/types/units/readings/statuses/thresholds and applicability
Stable mapping for every required processor sensor across IB SDR, IB Sensor List, OOB SDR, OOB Sensor List and Web row
Approved secure in-band/OOB access and Web capture path without plaintext credentials
Sampling alignment, freshness, rounding, unavailable/stale and Web pagination rules
Decision on the source's missing criteria numbers 3 through 5
Log retention policy, expected normal platform state and escalation owner
safety_requirements: Keep collection read-only and inject credentials through approved secret handling
Retain complete raw inventories before any CPU filter; never pass from grep/head-only evidence
Never assume the test title is a literal IPMI sensor name
Do not clear SEL, dmesg or syslog by default because doing so destroys evidence
Do not change thresholds, sensor policy, BMC configuration or processor state
Stop on ambiguous SUT/channel identity, missing/duplicate sensor, malformed/stale reading or security-policy violation
agent_execution_scope: Verify exact row/variant and collect complete read-only IB/OOB inventories
Apply only the owner-approved processor sensor map and normalize per-field semantics
Compare all mapped records and prepare Web rows/screenshots for review
Preserve raw logs, timestamps, command exits and discrepancies
Perform no credential disclosure, log clear, sensor writes, criteria invention or DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve processor topology, required sensor population, semantics and IB/OOB/Web mapping
Resolve the criteria-number jump and any additional omitted coverage
Review every per-sensor comparison and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A protected read-only ipmitool collector is applicable, but `sensor get 'Sensor Check - Processor'` substitutes a test title for real sensor identity; OOB-only collection, grep and `head -100` omit required channels and rows.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Using approved secret-safe access, retain full `sdr elist` and full `sensor list` output independently in-band and OOB, then select the owner-enumerated processor records and reconcile them with complete BMC-Web evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Both IB/OOB SDR and Sensor lists, BMC-Web Sensor list, SPEC comparison, anomaly review, Config-Check and 3/0-minute values remain; source log clearing is not executed automatically.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a versioned processor-sensor matrix keyed by physical socket/die and stable SDR record, collect four IPMI views plus Web at aligned times and compare every source-required field with the approved spec.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact topology, completeness, secure access, timestamp and semantic normalization while retaining every source channel.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A single successful sensor query cannot expose missing sensors, name/description drift, IB/OOB disagreement, Web pagination or unit/threshold differences.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Polling and Web caching can create transient differences; aligned timestamps and documented freshness/rounding rules are needed before classifying a discrepancy.

project_override_considerations: Projects may rename processor sensors only through a versioned physical-to-record/Web crosswalk. Any legitimately omitted criteria must be explicitly approved; the review cannot silently infer what numbers 3–5 meant.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, SUT/BMC/CPU topology and firmware/client identities
Versioned processor sensor specification and complete physical-to-IB/OOB/Web map
Complete redacted raw IB/OOB SDR and Sensor lists with timestamps and exit status
Complete BMC-Web sensor evidence including pagination and timestamps
Decision for criteria 3–5, preserved anomaly logs, no-write/no-clear audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master criteria jump from 2 to 6, leaving possible processor coverage undefined. DeepSeek also substitutes the test title for a sensor and omits required IB/Web and complete-list evidence. The known fields are preserved while the missing criteria are escalated.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The three-view processor sensor objective and safe passive evidence path are identifiable. Exact topology/specification and the criteria clarification are supplyable inputs, so review can complete without claiming execution readiness.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2011 Wistron-BMC-01032-V002: confirm whether Criteria numbering 1, 2, 6 is only a numbering typo or whether processor-sensor Criteria 3–5 are missing; if missing, provide their exact coverage, expected fields/values and IB/OOB/Web acceptance mapping while preserving all stated SDR, Sensor-List and BMC-Web checks.

review_improvement: Rejects the nonexistent title-based sensor shortcut, restores complete IB/OOB/Web population coverage and makes the skipped criteria explicit instead of silently reducing coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: Processor monitoring is a set-reconciliation problem, not a single-sensor lookup. The same physical CPU can appear under distinct SDR names or units across in-band, OOB and Web surfaces, and successful reading of one record cannot prove population completeness. Raw lists must remain untruncated so missing, extra and duplicate records are detectable. Because the source explicitly jumps to criterion 6, declaring full coverage without owner resolution would be an unjustified assumption.
